noun:Uhr.tx: From late Middle High German ūre, from Middle Low German ûre (“hour”), from Middle Dutch ûre, from Old Dutch *ūra, from Old French houre, from Latin hōra, from Ancient Greek ὥρα (hṓra), from Proto-Indo-European *yóh₁r̥ (“year, season”). The word was borrowed in the late 14th century when the diphthongization of -ū- into -ou-, -au- was already complete in most dialects; a shifted form exists, …

prep:um.tx: From Middle High German umbe, ümbe, from Old High German umbi, from Proto-West Germanic *umbi. Central German dialects show regular umlaut; the standard form is from Upper German, where umlaut of -u- was blocked before labial geminates and clusters. Cognate with Luxembourgish ëm, Dutch om.

conj:um.tx: From Middle High German umbe, ümbe, from Old High German umbi, from Proto-West Germanic *umbi. Central German dialects show regular umlaut; the standard form is from Upper German, where umlaut of -u- was blocked before labial geminates and clusters. Cognate with Luxembourgish ëm, Dutch om.

adj:um.tx: From Middle High German umbe, ümbe, from Old High German umbi, from Proto-West Germanic *umbi. Central German dialects show regular umlaut; the standard form is from Upper German, where umlaut of -u- was blocked before labial geminates and clusters. Cognate with Luxembourgish ëm, Dutch om.

adv:um.tx: From Middle High German umbe, ümbe, from Old High German umbi, from Proto-West Germanic *umbi. Central German dialects show regular umlaut; the standard form is from Upper German, where umlaut of -u- was blocked before labial geminates and clusters. Cognate with Luxembourgish ëm, Dutch om.

noun:UFO.tx: Borrowed from English UFO, initialism of unidentified flying object, itself translated into German as unidentifiziertes Flugobjekt or more commonly unbekanntes Flugobjekt.

noun:U-Bahn.tx: Short for Untergrundbahn ("underground railway"), but note that the first German underground, in Berlin, was initially called an Unterpflaster-Bahn ("underpavement railway"). Not to be confused with U-Straßenbahn (short for Undergrundstraßenbahn; in English known as premetro).

verb:übersetzen.tx: 16th century, from über- (“over”) + setzen (“to set”), probably modeled on Latin trādūcere, perhaps through Middle Low German ōversetten (15th c.).

prep:unter.tx: From Middle High German under, unter, from Old High German untar, from Proto-West Germanic *undar (compare Old Saxon undar, Hunsrik unne, Dutch onder, English under).

adj:übel.tx: Inherited from Middle High German übel, from Old High German ubil, from Proto-West Germanic *ubil. Compare Dutch euvel, English evil.

conj:und.tx: From Middle High German unde, from Old High German unti, from Proto-Germanic *andi, *anþi, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énti. Compare Dutch en, English and, Danish end.

intj:und.tx: From Middle High German unde, from Old High German unti, from Proto-Germanic *andi, *anþi, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énti. Compare Dutch en, English and, Danish end.

adv:überall.tx: From über + all. Compare English overall.

prep:über.tx: From Middle High German über, from Old High German ubiri, ubari, from Proto-Germanic *ubiri, from Proto-Indo-European *upéri, from *upér (ultimately from *upo + *-i). Cognate with Ancient Greek ὑπέρ (hupér, “above”), Latin super (“above”), Sanskrit उपरि (upári, “above, upper”), Hindi ऊपर (ūpar, “above, top, up”), Odia ଉପର (upara, “above, up”) and Punjabi ਉੱਪਰ (uppar, “above, top, up”). Akin to …

adj:über.tx: From Middle High German über, from Old High German ubiri, ubari, from Proto-Germanic *ubiri, from Proto-Indo-European *upéri, from *upér (ultimately from *upo + *-i). Cognate with Ancient Greek ὑπέρ (hupér, “above”), Latin super (“above”), Sanskrit उपरि (upári, “above, upper”), Hindi ऊपर (ūpar, “above, top, up”), Odia ଉପର (upara, “above, up”) and Punjabi ਉੱਪਰ (uppar, “above, top, up”). Akin to …

adv:über.tx: From Middle High German über, from Old High German ubiri, ubari, from Proto-Germanic *ubiri, from Proto-Indo-European *upéri, from *upér (ultimately from *upo + *-i). Cognate with Ancient Greek ὑπέρ (hupér, “above”), Latin super (“above”), Sanskrit उपरि (upári, “above, upper”), Hindi ऊपर (ūpar, “above, top, up”), Odia ଉପର (upara, “above, up”) and Punjabi ਉੱਪਰ (uppar, “above, top, up”). Akin to …

adv:ur.tx: From Middle High German ur-, from Old High German ur-, ir- (“thoroughly”), from Proto-Germanic *uz- (“out”).

noun:Übersetzung.tx: From the verb übersetzen + -ung. Compare Yiddish איבערזעצונג (iberzetsung), Alemannic German Übersetzig.

noun:Ultimatum.tx: From Medieval Latin ultimatus, from Late Latin ultimare (“to come to an end, be at the last”).

noun:Uniform.tx: Borrowed from French uniforme, from Latin uniformis.

noun:Union.tx: From French union, from Late Latin ūniō, from Latin ūnus (“one”).

noun:Ur.tx: 18th century, learned borrowing from Middle High German ūr(e), itself from Old High German ūro, from Proto-West Germanic *ūr. Displaced inherited Auer, which survives in the compound Auerochse.

noun:Uran.tx: Named after the planet Uranus, from Latin Ūranus.

noun:Übel.tx: From Middle High German übel n (synonym übele, übel f); more at übel. Cognate with English evil.

noun:Œuvre.tx: Borrowed from French œuvre. Doublet of Oper and Opus.

verb:urinieren.tx: From Medieval Latin urino + -ieren. Also analysable as Urin + -ieren.

verb:unterschreiben.tx: From Middle High German underschrīben, originally with separable prefix. Synchronically analyzable as unter- (“under”) + schreiben (“write”). Calque of Latin subscrībere.

noun:Unterschrift.tx: Derived from the verb unterschreiben (“to underwrite, sign”), equivalent to unter- + Schrift, literally “underwrit”. Cognate with Hunsrik Unnerschrift, German Low German Unnerschrift (“signature”).

verb:unterrichten.tx: From Middle High German underrihten, equivalent to unter- + richten. Cognate with Middle Low German underrichten (whence German Low German unnerrichten), Saterland Frisian unnergjuchte, and Dutch onderrichten.

noun:Unterricht.tx: From unterrichten; from Middle High German underrihten; unter- + richten.

verb:übertragen.tx: From Middle High German übertragen, at least in part a calque of Latin transferre. Analysable as über- (“over”) + tragen (“to carry”). Compare Dutch overdragen, English carry over.

noun:Universität.tx: Borrowed from Latin ūniversitās. By surface analysis, universitär + -ität. Compare Dutch universiteit.

noun:Unterseeboot.tx: Compound of unter + See + Boot, literally “under-sea boat”.

intj:uff.tx: An onomatopoeia. Similar to English oof and Dutch oef.

verb:umgehen.tx: From Middle High German umbegēn, umbegān, from Old High German umbigēn, umbigān, from Proto-West Germanic *umbigān, from Proto-Germanic *umbigāną. Equivalent to um- + gehen.

noun:Ufer.tx: From Middle High German uover, ūver, ūber, possibly from northern Old High German *uofar, but usually considered a borrowing from Middle Low German ōver, ȫver, from Old Saxon *ōvar, *ōvir, from Proto-Germanic *ōferaz. Cognate with Dutch oever, Low German Över, English over (“shore, riverbank”). The native High German word for “shore” is Gestade.

adv:unterwegs.tx: From older unterwegen, from Middle High German under wegen, from Old High German untar wegun. Equivalent to unter- (“under”) + Weg (“way”) + -s (adverbial suffix). Compare Dutch onderweg, English underway.

noun:Ulme.tx: Conflation of Middle High German elm, from Old High German elm, from Proto-West Germanic *elm (“elm”), and Latin ulmus (“elm”).

noun:Urlaub.tx: From Middle High German urloup. Related to erlauben. Cognate with English leave (“time off, permission to be away”).

noun:Urteil.tx: From Middle High German urteil, from Old High German urteil, urteili, from Proto-Germanic *uzdailiją (“judicial decision; verdict; judgement”). Cognate with Dutch oordeel and English ordeal.

adv:unten.tx: From Middle High German unden(e), undenen, und(e)nân, untnân, from Old High German undenân, untenân, untana. Related to unter.

noun:Unterschied.tx: From the fusion of Middle High German underschiet, underschit, Middle High German underschide, and Middle High German underscheit, unterscheid, from Old High German untarskeit, untarskeid; derived synchronically from unterscheiden. Compare Dutch onderscheid, Hunsrik Unnerschied, Low German Ünnerscheed, Saterland Frisian Unnerskeed.

noun:Umwelt.tx: From um- + Welt. In the biological sense first used by Jakob Johann von Uexküll (1909).

noun:Unterhose.tx: From unter- (“under”) + Hose (“trousers”). Cognate with Hunsrik Unnerhoss.

intj:Uppsala.tx: Blend of ups (“oops”) + hoppala (“oops”), influenced by the Swedish city.

det:unser.tx: From Middle High German unser, from Old High German unsēr, from Proto-West Germanic *unsar.

noun:Uhu.tx: Like obsolete Buhu, Schuhu, an alteration of early modern German Huhu, itself an onomatopoeic reduplication of *Hu, from Middle High German hūwe, huo, from Old High German hūwo (“nightowl”), from Proto-West Germanic *hūō (“owl”).

noun:Unze.tx: From Middle High German unz, unze, from Old High German unza, from Proto-West Germanic *unciju (“ounce; unit of money”).

adj:überflüssig.tx: Calque of Late Latin superfluus, über- + flüssig.

adv:überflüssig.tx: Calque of Late Latin superfluus, über- + flüssig.

adj:unheimlich.tx: From Middle High German unheimlich, from Old High German *unheimlīh, equivalent to un- + heimlich (“familiar”).

adv:unheimlich.tx: From Middle High German unheimlich, from Old High German *unheimlīh, equivalent to un- + heimlich (“familiar”).

adv:übermorgen.tx: Inherited from Middle High German übermorgen, from Old High German ubar morgan, ubar morgana; equivalent to über- (“over, above”) + morgen (“tomorrow”). Compare Dutch overmorgen, Yiddish איבערמאָרגן (ibermorgn).

verb:unterbrechen.tx: From Middle High German underbrëchen, from Old High German untarbrëhhan, a calque of Latin interrumpere. By surface analysis, unter- + brechen. Compare Dutch onderbreken.

noun:Unwetter.tx: From Middle High German unweter, unwiter, from Old High German unwetar, from Proto-Germanic *unwedrą. By surface analysis, un- (“bad, grave”) + Wetter (“weather”). Cognate with Dutch onweer, English unweather, Swedish oväder, among others.

noun:Untermensch.tx: 18th century, from unter- (“under, sub”) + Mensch (“human being”).

noun:Untergang.tx: From Old High German untargang. By surface analysis, unter + Gang; cognate with Hunsrik Unnergang, Luxembourgish Ënnergang, German Low German Ünnergang.

noun:Umfang.tx: From Middle High German umbefanc, umbevanc, equivalent to um- + Fang. Compare Middle Low German ümmevanc, German Low German Ümfang, Dutch omvang.

adj:uralt.tx: From Middle High German uralt, from Old High German uralt, from Proto-West Germanic [Term?]. Compare Dutch oeroud, Old English oreald. Equivalent to ur- + alt.

noun:Unterdrückung.tx: From unterdrücken (“to oppress”) + -ung. Compare Dutch onderdrukking, Danish undertrykkelse, Norwegian Bokmål undertrykkelse.

noun:Utopie.tx: Borrowed from French utopie, from English utopia, which see for more.

adj:überlegen.tx: From Middle High German überlegen, past participle of überligen. By surface analysis, über + gelegen.

verb:überlegen.tx: From Middle High German überlegen, from Old High German ubarleggen, from Proto-West Germanic *ubirlaggjan, from Proto-Germanic *uberlagjaną. Equivalent to über- + legen. Cognate with Dutch overleggen and English overlay.

noun:Unke.tx: From Middle High German unc (“snake, basilisk”), from Old High German unc (“snake”), from Proto-Germanic *ungwô, *unkaz (“snake, adder”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂n̥gʷʰ-, zero-grade stem of *h₂éngʷʰis (compare Latin anguis, Lithuanian angi̇̀s). The sense may have been influenced by obsolete Eutze (“toad”) (modern Bavarian Hötsch).

verb:überraschen.tx: über- + raschen, compare Low German overraschen, överraschen, English over-, rush. Compare also Middle Low German vorraschen, vörraschen (“to take by surprise”).

verb:überwältigen.tx: From über- + wältigen. Related to Gewalt (power, might).

noun:Umschlag.tx: Deverbal from umschlagen. Compare the noun Umschlagen, nominalisation of the same verb.

noun:Untersuchung.tx: From untersuchen + -ung; cognate with Hunsrik Unnersuchung.

verb:untersuchen.tx: First attested in the 15th century as undersuochen. This form suggests that it had already existed as Middle High German *undersuochen. The existence of an unattested Old High German form *untarsuohhen is probable, compare Old Saxon undarsōkian (whence Low German ünnersöken), Old Dutch undersuoken (whence Dutch onderzoeken), and Old English undersēċan (whence English underseek), all from …

verb:üben.tx: From Middle High German üeben, uoben, from Old High German uoben, from Proto-Germanic *ōbijaną (“to do, practice”).

adv:üben.tx: Formed from über (“across”) by analogy to pairs like unter - unten, ober - oben.

noun:Übung.tx: From Middle High German üebunge, from Old High German uobunga. Equivalent to üben + -ung.

noun:Unding.tx: From Middle High German undinc, undinge, equivalent to un- + Ding (“thing”). Compare Dutch onding, West Frisian ûnding, English unthing.

noun:Unfall.tx: From Middle High German unval, ungeval. Analysable as un- (“bad, grave”) + Fall (“case, situation”). Compare Dutch ongeval.

verb:unterscheiden.tx: From Middle High German underscheiden; equivalent to unter- + scheiden. Compare Dutch onderscheiden.

verb:unterwerfen.tx: From unter- + werfen. Compare Dutch onderwerpen.

adj:unmöglich.tx: un- + möglich; cognate with Hunsrik unmeeghlich, Old Danish umugh(i)likær, Old Norse úmǫguligr, and Old Swedish ōmø̄gheliker

adv:unmöglich.tx: un- + möglich; cognate with Hunsrik unmeeghlich, Old Danish umugh(i)likær, Old Norse úmǫguligr, and Old Swedish ōmø̄gheliker

adv:überhaupt.tx: From Middle High German überhoubet, equivalent to über- + Haupt.

noun:Unterwelt.tx: 15th century, from unter- + Welt. The sense “world of crime” (early 20th c.) is a semantic loan from English underworld.

noun:Überschuss.tx: From Early New High German überschus, überschuz. By surface analysis, deverbal from überschießen. Also analyzable as über- + Schuss.

adj:unmittelbar.tx: From un- (“un-”) + Mittel (“means, medium”) + -bar (“-able, -ly”), 17th-century alteration of Middle High German unmittelich, calque of Latin immediatus, itself a calque of Ancient Greek ἄμεσος (ámesos).

adj:ungefähr.tx: From Middle High German ân gevœre, mostly Middle High German ân gevœrde (“without evil intention, without deceit”). Equivalent to ohne (“without”) + Gefahr (“threat, danger, peril”). Cognate with Dutch ongeveer.

adv:ungefähr.tx: From Middle High German ân gevœre, mostly Middle High German ân gevœrde (“without evil intention, without deceit”). Equivalent to ohne (“without”) + Gefahr (“threat, danger, peril”). Cognate with Dutch ongeveer.

noun:Unglück.tx: From Middle High German unglück, unglücke, ungelücke, equivalent to un- + Glück (“luck”). Compare Dutch ongeluk.

noun:Unsinn.tx: From Middle High German unsin (“nonsense, folly”) (compare Middle High German unsinne (“ignorance, stupidity”)), equivalent to un- + Sinn.

verb:unterhalten.tx: From the 17th century, from unter + halten. Possibly a calque of French entretenir. Cognate with Hunsrik unnerhalle.

verb:untergehen.tx: From Middle High German undergēn, undergān, from Old High German untargēn, untargān, from Proto-West Germanic *undergān. Equivalent to unter- + gehen; cognate with Hunsrik unnergehn, and literally with English undergo.

verb:umbringen.tx: From Middle High German umbebringen, from Old High German umbibringan. Equivalent to um- + bringen. Compare Dutch ombrengen.

noun:Umstand.tx: From Middle High German umbestand (literally “a standing around; an umb-stand”), a Germanic calque of Latin circumstans (whence English circumstance), which is circum (“about”) + stans (“standing”). By surface analysis, um- + Stand.

verb:überfallen.tx: From Middle High German übervallen, equivalent to über- + fallen. Cognate with Middle Low German ȫvervallen (> German Low German overfallen, överfallen), English overfall.

noun:Überfall.tx: Deverbal from überfallen, notably with a stress change. Compare Dutch overval.

adj:unerklärlich.tx: un- + erklärlich, the latter from erklären + -lich.

adj:unruhig.tx: From un- + ruhig. Cognate with Hunsrik unruhich.

adv:unruhig.tx: From un- + ruhig. Cognate with Hunsrik unruhich.

noun:Ursache.tx: From Middle High German ursache. Equivalent to ur- + Sache.

adj:ursprünglich.tx: From Middle High German ursprunclich. Equivalent to Ursprung + -lich.

noun:Unkraut.tx: From Middle High German and Old High German unkrūt, corresponding to un- + Kraut. Compare Dutch onkruid.

verb:umleiten.tx: From Middle High German umbeleiten, from Old High German umbileiten, from Proto-West Germanic *umbilaidijan. Equivalent to um- + leiten.

verb:unterlegen.tx: From Middle High German underlegen, from Old High German untarleggen, from Proto-West Germanic *undarlaggjan. Equivalent to unter- + legen.

noun:Umhang.tx: From Middle High German umbehanc, from Old High German [Term?].

verb:überleben.tx: über- + leben, a calque of Latin supervīvō.

verb:übertreiben.tx: Inherited from Middle High German übertrīben, equivalent to über- + treiben

adj:untreu.tx: From Middle High German untriuwe, from Old High German ungitriuwi, urtriuwi, *untriuwi, from Proto-West Germanic *untriuwī, from Proto-Germanic *untriwwiz. Equivalent to un- + treu.

verb:urteilen.tx: From Middle High German urteilen, denominative from Urteil + -en, displacing synonymous erteilen.

adj:unaussprechlich.tx: From un- + aussprechen + -lich. First attested as unûzsprechelich in spiritual literature of the 14th century, modelled after terms such as Ancient Greek ἀνεκφώνητος (anekphṓnētos), ἀνεκδιήγητος (anekdiḗgētos) and Latin ineffabilis.

noun:Umgebung.tx: From umgeben + -ung. Cognate with Dutch omgeving.

adj:ungestüm.tx: From Middle High German ungestüeme, Old High German ungistuomi (“stormy, impetuous”), negation of *gistuomi (“still, gentle”), from *gistemmen (“to halt”), ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *stammijan (“to stop”).

adj:unehrlich.tx: From Middle High German [Term?]; un- + ehrlich. Cognate with Hunsrik uneherlich.

noun:Überfluss.tx: From Middle High German [Term?]. Equivalent to über- + Fluss.

adj:üppig.tx: From Middle High German üppic, from Old High German uppīg, further origin uncertain, perhaps related to übel.

adv:üppig.tx: From Middle High German üppic, from Old High German uppīg, further origin uncertain, perhaps related to übel.

adj:unfähig.tx: un- (“un-”) + fähig (“able, capable”); cognate with Hunsrik unfähich

noun:Uhrzeit.tx: From Uhr (“clock”) + Zeit (“time”). Cognate with Hunsrik Uherzeid.

verb:überwinden.tx: From Middle High German überwinden, from Old High German ubarwintan, an originally Upper German form besides Central German überwinnen, ubarwinnan. This latter is from Proto-West Germanic *ubarwinnan. Cognate with Dutch overwinnen, English overwin. Equivalent to über- + winnen (“to win”, simplex of gewinnen). The form with -nd- is analysable as über- + winden (“to wind, twist”). It is uncertain …

verb:übernachten.tx: From Middle High German übernahten, from Old High German ubarnahtēn (“to overnight”), from Proto-West Germanic *obarnahtēn (“to overnight”), equivalent to über- + Nacht + -en. Cognate with German Low German övernachten, Dutch overnachten, West Frisian oernachtsje, Saterland Frisian uurnoachtje, English overnight.

adj:untertan.tx: From Middle High German undertān, from Old High German untartān, past participle of the verb untartuon ("to subdue").

adj:unglücklich.tx: From un- + glücklich; cognate with Hunsrik unglicklich.

adv:unglücklich.tx: From un- + glücklich; cognate with Hunsrik unglicklich.

adj:überheblich.tx: überheben (“to overstrain oneself”) + -lich, which could be compared to English overheave.

noun:Uhrzeigersinn.tx: From Uhrzeiger (“clock hand”) + Sinn. The latter word is used here in the archaic sense “way, direction”.

adj:ungehorsam.tx: From Middle High German ungehōrsam, from Old High German *ungihōrsam, from Proto-West Germanic *ungahauʀisam. Equivalent to un- + gehorsam.

adj:übrig.tx: From Middle High German überec. Compare Dutch overig. Equivalent to über + -ig.

verb:überschreiten.tx: über- + schreiten. Compare Dutch overschrijden, Swedish överskrida, Danish overskride, Norwegian Bokmål overskride.

verb:überhitzen.tx: From Middle High German überhitzen, equivalent to über- + Hitze + -en.

noun:Ungeziefer.tx: From early modern German ungeziffer, Ungezieffer, a variant form of Middle High German ungezibere. These pertain to Old High German zebar (“sacrificial animal”) and hence originally meant “animals unsuitable for sacrifice”, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *tībrą (“offering, sacrifice, victim”). The word is rarely attested in medieval texts due to suppression of words reminiscent of heathen …

noun:Urschrei.tx: From ur- (“primitive, original”) + Schrei (“shout, cry, scream”).

verb:unterliegen.tx: From Middle High German unterligen, from Old High German untarliggan (“to lie beneath”), equivalent to unter- + liegen. More at underlie.

noun:Umweg.tx: From Middle High German *ummewëc, umbewëc, from Middle High German umbe (“around”) + wëc (“way”); equivalent to um- + Weg.

noun:Ursprung.tx: From Middle High German ursprunc, from Old High German ursprung. By surface analysis, ur- + Sprung. Compare Dutch oorsprong.

pt: to overflow, to overrun, to defect
noun:Überläufer.tx: From überlaufen (“to overflow, to overrun, to defect”) + -er

noun:Urkunde.tx: Middle High German urkunde f, urkünde n, from Old High German urkundī f, (much more common) urkundi n (8th century). Compare Dutch oorkonde, from Middle Dutch oorconde, orconde, from Middle Low German ōrkunde. From the same roots as, though not directly a compound, of ur- + Kunde.

adj:ungeheuer.tx: Middle High German ungehiure, Old High German ungihiuri, un- + geheuer

adv:ungeheuer.tx: Middle High German ungehiure, Old High German ungihiuri, un- + geheuer

noun:Unfug.tx: From Middle High German unvuoc, equivalent to un- + Fug. Cognate with Swedish ofog.

noun:Übergriff.tx: From Late Middle High German [Term?], from Old High German [Term?]; über- + Griff. Compare the noun Übergreifen, nominalisation of the verb übergreifen.

noun:Ungenauigkeit.tx: From un- + Genauigkeit; equivalent to ungenau + -igkeit.

noun:Usus.tx: Borrowed from Latin ūsus, originally student slang.

noun:Unterhalt.tx: Deverbal nominal form of unterhalten (“to maintain”).

noun:Unterrock.tx: From Middle High German underroc, *unterroc, equivalent to unter- + Rock.

verb:umfahren.tx: From Middle High German umbevarn, from Old High German umbifaran, from Proto-West Germanic *umbifaran. Equivalent to um- + fahren.

verb:überholen.tx: From Middle High German überholn. Analyzable as über- + holen.

noun:Übermacht.tx: By surface analysis, über- (“over-, hyper-”) + Macht (“might, power”). Compare Dutch overmacht, oppermacht.

verb:unterlassen.tx: From Middle High German underlāȥen, from Old High German untarlāȥan. Equivalent to unter- + lassen.

noun:Uhrmacher.tx: From Uhr (“watch, clock”) + Macher (“maker, producer”). Cognate with Hunsrik Uhermacher.

noun:Übergang.tx: From Middle High German überganc, from Old High German ubargang. Cognate to Dutch overgang.

verb:überdenken.tx: From über- + denken. Compare archaic English overthink.

adj:unverschämt.tx: un- (“un-”) + verschämt (“bashful, shy”), with semantic shift "not shy" > "rude, insolent".

noun:Unikat.tx: From Latin ūnicus + -at, following the pattern of Duplikat (“duplicate”).

adj:ungeduldig.tx: From Middle High German ungedultic, from Old High German ungidultīg. By surface analysis, Ungeduld + -ig or un- + geduldig.

adv:ungeduldig.tx: From Middle High German ungedultic, from Old High German ungidultīg. By surface analysis, Ungeduld + -ig or un- + geduldig.

adj:unschuldig.tx: From un- + schuldig, the latter from Schuld + -ig.

noun:Unterkunft.tx: From the verb unterkommen (“to find a place, find shelter”).

adj:unhaltbar.tx: From un- + haltbar and further from un- + halten + -bar.

verb:überreden.tx: From Middle High German überreden. Equivalent to über- (“over”) + reden (“talk”).

verb:umkommen.tx: From Middle High German umbekomen (“to pass by, end, die”). Analysable as um- + kommen. Cognate with Middle Dutch ommecomen (“to pass by, end, die”), whence modern Dutch omkomen. Compare also ums Leben kommen, and further umbringen, ums Leben bringen. Regarding the broader semantic use in both Middle High German and Middle Dutch, it is not certain that the short verbs are mere ellipses of the …

verb:umschreiben.tx: From um (“around, re-”) + schreiben (“to write”). Probably after Latin trānscrībere in the sense of “transcribe”, perhaps also in some other senses.

adj:ultimativ.tx: First attested in the first half of the 20th century. Compare French ultimatif and Dutch ultimatief.

adv:ultimativ.tx: First attested in the first half of the 20th century. Compare French ultimatif and Dutch ultimatief.

adj:unrecht.tx: From Old High German unreht, from Proto-Germanic *unrehtaz. Cognate with English unright, Dutch onrecht.

noun:Unterbewusstsein.tx: From unterbewusst + Sein or rather unter- + Bewusstsein.

verb:überkommen.tx: From Middle High German überkomen, from Old High German ubarqueman. By surface analysis, über- + kommen.

verb:umkehren.tx: From Middle High German ummekēren, umbekēren, from Old High German umbikēren, from Proto-West Germanic *umbikaʀʀjan. Equivalent to um- (“round”) + kehren (“turn”). Cognate with Middle Low German ümmekēren, Dutch omkeren, Old English ymbċierran (“to turn about, revolve”).

verb:übergeben.tx: über- + geben. Cognate with English overgive. Compare Dutch overgeven, which can also mean "to vomit" as well.

adj:unrein.tx: From Middle High German [Term?], from Old High German unreini, from Proto-West Germanic *unhrainī, from Proto-Germanic *unhrainiz; equivalent to un- + rein.

adj:unsinnig.tx: Middle High German unsinnec, Old High German unsinnīg, corresponding to un- + sinnig.

adv:unsinnig.tx: Middle High German unsinnec, Old High German unsinnīg, corresponding to un- + sinnig.

noun:Untiefe.tx: Formally un- (“un-”) + Tiefe (“depth”). The nautical sense “shallows” is chiefly from Middle Low German undēpe (compare Dutch ondiepte (“shallows”)). It is also attested in Old High German untiufī, but seemingly not in Middle High German. In the sense “abyss”, the prefix un- takes the meaning “inconceivable” as, for example, in Unding (“absurdity, deformity”). It is first attested in Middle High …

noun:Unterführung.tx: From the verb unterführen. By surface analysis, unterführen + -ung or unter- + Führung.

verb:unternehmen.tx: From Middle High German undernëmen, from Old High German untarnëman, from Proto-West Germanic *underneman. Equivalent to unter- + nehmen. Cognate to Dutch ondernemen and obsolete English undernim. Modern meaning first attested in the 16th century.

verb:überführen.tx: From über- + führen. Cognate with Dutch overvoeren. Compare also English overfare.

verb:umlegen.tx: From Middle High German umbelegen, from Old High German umbileggen, from Proto-West Germanic *umbilaggjan. Equivalent to um- + legen. Cognate to Dutch omleggen.

adj:urbar.tx: In the modern sense (18th century) via Low German from Middle Low German *ōrbār (in ōrbārheit), Middle Dutch ōrbare (“fruitful”), derived from the noun ōrbār, from Old Saxon ur- + beran (“to bear”), cognate of modern German Urbar (“urbarium”, originally “yield, benefit, fee”), which see for more. An unrelated derivation from the same noun was Upper German urbor (“liable to taxation”).

verb:überschreiben.tx: From über- + schreiben (inseparable) or über + schreiben (separable).

noun:Umgang.tx: From Middle High German umbeganc, from Old High German umbigang (“a course, return”), from Proto-Germanic *umbigangaz (“a going around, circuit”), equivalent to um- + Gang (“a gang, going”). Cognate with Dutch omgang, English umgang, Danish omgang, Swedish omgång, Norwegian omgang.

adj:unleserlich.tx: From un- + leserlich. Further analysable as un- + lesen + -er- + -lich.

noun:Umsatz.tx: Borrowed from Middle Low German ummesat, from the verb ummesetten (modern Standard High German: umsetzen).

noun:Überzug.tx: Ablaut to überziehen or über- + Zug. Already Old High German ubarzug but mostly new formations in New High German.

adj:unerheblich.tx: un- + erheblich. Originally meaning "which cannot be lifted", this word was later equated with Latin irrelevāns and Italian irrelevante.

noun:Umpolung.tx: From umpolen + -ung; equivalent to um- + Polung.

verb:umhüllen.tx: From Middle High German umbehüllen, from Old High German umbihullen. Equivalent to um- + hüllen.

verb:umsetzen.tx: From um- + setzen. Cognate with Middle English umsetten (“to surround, beset”), English umbeset.

noun:Unmut.tx: From Middle High German unmuot, from Old High German unmuot; equivalent to un- + Mut.

noun:Überbleibsel.tx: 17th century, from überbleiben (“to remain”) + -sel, likely after Dutch and Middle Dutch overblijfsel.

adj:ungut.tx: From Middle High German and Old High German unguot. By surface analysis, un- + gut. Compare English ungood, obsolete Dutch ongoed.

noun:Übermut.tx: From Middle High German übermuot, from Old High German ubarmuot, ubermuot. By surface analysis, über- + Mut.

adj:unkaputtbar.tx: From un- + kaputt + -bar. The word was used first in 1990 in an advertising campaign. It intentionally violates the grammar rules by using the suffix -bar with the adjective kaputt despite the fact that this suffix is only used to build adjectives from verbs (e.g. unkaputtmachbar). This made the word sound somewhat funny with the purpose of drawing attention.

adj:undankbar.tx: From un- + dankbar or un- + Dank + -bar.

noun:Unterlage.tx: Verbal noun of unterliegen, equivalent to unter- (“under”) + Lage (“position, lying, layer”). Middle High German underlāge is already attested, but only in the sense of “being defeated” (still present in the verb unterliegen, but long lost in the noun; compare Niederlage). The sense “document” from the notion of “papers used as basis, support”.

verb:untersagen.tx: From Middle High German undersagen, from Old High German untarsagēn. Equivalent to unter- + sagen.

adv:unseretwegen.tx: Previously more common as unsertwegen, the form unseretwegen likely became dominate out of assimilation to the construction -etwegen as in meinetwegen, deinetwegen, etc. Shortened from von unseretwegen, which can be traced through two developmental routes. One route is from von unsernt / unsrent / unserent wegen, from von unseren wegen, from Middle High German von unsern wegen, in which wegen was …

adj:überladen.tx: Past participle of the above verb.

noun:Unbekannte.tx: Substantivisation of unbekannt and shorting of unbekannte Größe, known in Latin as quantitas incognita

noun:Unschuld.tx: From Middle High German unschult, unschulde, from Old High German unskuld, unsculd. Equivalent to un- + Schuld.

adj:unverhohlen.tx: From the old participal construction verhohlen and the prefix un-. The first word stems from Middle High German verheln, from Old High German firhelan. In this adjective the former conjugation as class 4 strong verb survives.

noun:Untermenü.tx: From unter- + Menü. Calque of English submenu.

adj:unbescholten.tx: From Middle High German unbescholten, the negated past participle of Middle High German beschelten, from Old High German biskeltan, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *skeldaną.

verb:unterstehen.tx: From Middle High German understān, understēn. Compare Low German onderstaan, English understand. By surface analysis, unter- + stehen.

adj:ungleich.tx: From Old High German ungilīh, from Proto-Germanic *ungalīkaz. By surface analysis, un- + gleich. Compare Old English unġelīċ (English unlike), Dutch ongelijk, Old Norse úlíkr (see there for North Germanic descendants).

adv:ungleich.tx: From Old High German ungilīh, from Proto-Germanic *ungalīkaz. By surface analysis, un- + gleich. Compare Old English unġelīċ (English unlike), Dutch ongelijk, Old Norse úlíkr (see there for North Germanic descendants).

adj:unverfroren.tx: Borrowed from German Low German [Term?]. Analysable as un- + verfroren, literally “not frozen, not chilled to the bone”. It is supposed that the word is eventually a modification of Middle Low German unvervērt (“fearless”). Compare Dutch onvervaard and Norwegian Bokmål forferde, forferdelig (related to German Gefahr, English fear). While that is uncertain, the form unverfroren is definitely based …

adv:unverfroren.tx: Borrowed from German Low German [Term?]. Analysable as un- + verfroren, literally “not frozen, not chilled to the bone”. It is supposed that the word is eventually a modification of Middle Low German unvervērt (“fearless”). Compare Dutch onvervaard and Norwegian Bokmål forferde, forferdelig (related to German Gefahr, English fear). While that is uncertain, the form unverfroren is definitely based …

noun:Urbar.tx: From Middle High German urbar, urbor, from Old High German urberan (“to bring, to create”), from ur- + beran (“to carry”) (compare English bear).

adj:unversehrt.tx: From un- (“un-, not”) + versehrt (“hurt, wounded”, past participle of versehren (“to hurt, to wound”)).

noun:Uchte.tx: Borrowed from Middle Low German uchte, from Old Saxon ūhta, from Proto-Germanic *unhtwǭ. Related to Dutch ochtend (“morning”).

noun:Untier.tx: From Middle High German untier, equivalent to un- + Tier. Cognate with German Low German Undeer, Dutch ondier, West Frisian ûndier.

verb:überbrücken.tx: über- + brücken. Inherited from Middle High German überbrücken, compare Dutch overbruggen, Swedish överbrygga, Old English oferbrycgian.

noun:Untat.tx: From Middle High German untāt, from Old High German untāt, from Proto-Germanic *undēdiz. Analysable as un- (“bad, grave”) + Tat (“deed”). Cognate with Middle Dutch ondaet, Middle Low German undāt, Old English undǣd.

noun:Undank.tx: From Middle High German undanc, from Old High German undank, undanc (“unthankfulness”), from Proto-West Germanic *unþank, from Proto-Germanic *unþankaz, equivalent to un- + Dank. Cognate with Dutch ondank, Old English unþanc ("unfavour, unpleasure, anger, ill-will"; whence modern English unthank).

adj:unehelich.tx: un- (“un-”) + ehelich (“marital”), further analyzable as un- (“un-”) + Ehe (“marriage”) + -lich (“-ly”)

noun:Unterseite.tx: From unter or unter- and Seite.

noun:Unzucht.tx: From Middle High German unzuht (“immorality, vulgarity, rudeness”), from Old High German unzuht, by surface analysis, un- + Zucht. Zucht originally means “discipline, education, manners”. Unzucht is derived thence, but was often restricted to the sexual sense already in early modern German. The simplex Zucht only later developed the additional sense “breeding”, with which Unzucht is now …

adj:unbedarft.tx: First attested around 1900, borrowed from Low German unbedarvd (“clumsy”), from Middle Low German unbederve, unbedarve (“weak, clumsy”), ultimately from Middle Low German bederven, bedarven (“to need, to require”).

noun:Unhold.tx: From Middle High German unholde, from Old High German unholdo, from Proto-West Germanic *unholþō, from Proto-Germanic *unhulþô. The regional sense “rascal” is chiefly from Low German (Middle Low German unholt). It is possible that the word was influenced here by unrelated holden (“to hold”), thus with the notion of “someone unheld, ungovernable”. Compare the synonym Unband.

verb:unterkommen.tx: From Middle High German underkomen, from Old High German untarqueman, from Proto-West Germanic *underkweman. Equivalent to unter- + kommen.

adj:überkandidelt.tx: Partial calque of Low German överkandidelt (19th c.), from kandidel (“cheerful”), itself plausibly from Latin candidus (“clear, bright”, hence “untarnished, untroubled”).

adj:unerbittlich.tx: Inherited from Middle High German unerbitlich, from Old High German unirbëtanlīh, equivalent to un- + erbitten + -lich. Compare Dutch oneerbiedig.

adv:unerbittlich.tx: Inherited from Middle High German unerbitlich, from Old High German unirbëtanlīh, equivalent to un- + erbitten + -lich. Compare Dutch oneerbiedig.

adj:unkundig.tx: From Middle High German unkundic, unkündic, from Old High German unkundīg, from Proto-West Germanic *unkunþīg, from Proto-Germanic *unkunþīgaz, equivalent to un- + kundig.

adj:unausstehlich.tx: Analyzable as un- + ausstehlich, although ausstehlich is possibly a back-formation of unausstehlich, in which case it would be preferable to analyze as un- + ausstehen + -lich.

adj:unleugbar.tx: Equivalent to un- + leugbar. See the latter.

adj:unnütz.tx: Inherited from Middle High German unnütze, unnutze, from Old High German unnuzzi. By surface analysis, un- + nütz

adj:unumgänglich.tx: From un- + umgänglich. Possibly a calque of Latin necessārius.

noun:Ulan.tx: Borrowed from Polish ułan, from Turkish oğlan.

adj:unweigerlich.tx: From Middle High German unweigerlīche, from un- + weigerlich; see weigern (“to refuse”).

adv:unweigerlich.tx: From Middle High German unweigerlīche, from un- + weigerlich; see weigern (“to refuse”).

adj:unwirsch.tx: Contracted from Middle High German unwirdisch (“showing or deserving contempt”). Equivalent to Unwürde (“dishonour”) + -isch.

noun:Unflat.tx: From Middle High German unvlāt, unvlāte, from Old High German *unflāt, from Proto-West Germanic *unflādi (“impurity, dirt, filth”).

verb:umzäunen.tx: From Middle High German umbzūnen, umbeziunen, equivalent to um- + zäunen. Compare Middle Low German ümmetünen.

verb:übertreten.tx: From Middle High German übertreten. By surface analysis, über (“over”) + treten (“to step”).

noun:USB-Stick.tx: From rarer English USB stick. Compare commoner English USB drive and memory stick.

verb:überrunden.tx: From either über- (“over-”) + runden (“to make round”) or rather directly from the noun Runde (“round, lap”). The simplex verb has no really fitting sense, but compare umrunden (“to circle, move around”).

verb:umwerfen.tx: From Middle High German umbewerfen. By surface analysis, um- + werfen.

verb:übersteigen.tx: From Old High German ubarstīgan. Cognate with Dutch overstijgen, Old English oferstīgan, Gothic 𐌿𐍆𐌰𐍂𐍃𐍄𐌴𐌹𐌲𐌰𐌽 (ufarsteigan). Equivalent to über- + steigen.

noun:Unwissenheit.tx: From unwissend + -heit. The elision of the d is regular, compare Abwesenheit, Zuvorkommenheit etc.

verb:übervorteilen.tx: 15th century, from über- (“over-”) + Vorteil (“advantage”) + -en, meaning “to seek an [undue] advantage over”.

verb:unterweisen.tx: unter- + weisen. Compare Dutch onderwijzen and West Frisian ûnderwize.

verb:überwintern.tx: From über + Winter + -n. Compare Dutch overwinteren, English overwinter.

adj:übermütig.tx: From Middle High German übermüetec, from Old High German ubarmuotīg. Equivalent to Übermut + -ig.

noun:Ud.tx: Borrowed from Arabic عُود (ʕūd). Doublet of Laute.

noun:Ungetüm.tx: Equivalent to un- + ge- + -tum. Cognate with Old English undōm (“injustice”).

verb:untergraben.tx: From Middle High German undergraben, from Old High German untargraban. Equivalent to unter- + graben. Cognate with Dutch ondergraven.

verb:unterbinden.tx: From Middle High German underbinden, from Old High German untarbintan. Equivalent to unter- + binden. Cognate to Dutch onderbinden.

noun:Unrat.tx: From un- + Rat, change of meaning in Middle High German.

noun:Ukulele.tx: From English ukulele, from Hawaiian ʻukulele, from ʻuku (“flea”) + lele (“jump, jumping”).

noun:Unsitte.tx: From Middle High German unsite, from Old High German unsitu. By surface analysis, un- + Sitte. Compare Old English unsidu.

noun:Unzahl.tx: un- + Zahl. Compare with Swedish otal, Danish utal, Norwegian utall.

verb:übersiedeln.tx: From über + siedeln (separable) or über- + siedeln (inseparable).

noun:Untersatz.tx: unter (“under, beneath”); deverbal from setzen (“place, put”)

noun:Unkosten.tx: 15th century, from un- + Kosten, literally “un-costs”, i.e. “bad costs” (with the prefix used as in Unmensch). At first Central German, surely after earlier Middle Low German unkost or Middle Dutch oncost (1372).

noun:Unstern.tx: From un- + Stern, calque of French désastre.

noun:Unterstand.tx: From Middle High German unterstant, from understēn, and new formations from descendant unterstehen in both stress patterns; in the sense of a subject calque of Latin subiectum; in the sense of a sub-class in society unter- + Stand.

verb:übertünchen.tx: From über- + tünchen (inseparable) or über + tünchen (separable).

noun:Überschlag.tx: Derived from überschlagen, equivalent to über- + Schlag.

noun:Urvertrauen.tx: ur- (“original”) + Vertrauen (“trust”), coined as a translation of basic trust in psychological literature.

noun:Ungestüm.tx: From Middle High German ungestüeme n or f, from Old High German ungistuomi n and ungistuomī f, nominalisations of the adjective ungistuomi, whence modern ungestüm.

noun:Umschweif.tx: From Middle High German umbesweif, from Old High German umbisweift.

noun:Unfriede.tx: From Middle High German unvride, from Old High German unfridu, from Proto-West Germanic *unfriþu, from Proto-Germanic *unfriþuz. By surface analysis, un- + Friede. Compare Dutch onvrede, Old English unfriþ. Also compare to modern English fray ("conflict, quarrel, heated argument,") which derives by aphesis from affray—an Old French loan—ultimately equivalent to a compound of French é- ("out, away …

verb:umbinden.tx: From Middle High German umbebinden, from Old High German *umbibintan, from Proto-West Germanic *umbibindan. Equivalent to um- + binden. Compare Dutch ombinden.

verb:umringen.tx: From Middle High German umberingen, from Old High German umbiringen, umbihringen, from Proto-West Germanic *umbihringan. By surface analysis, um- + Ring + -en. Compare Dutch omringen.

noun:Unzeit.tx: From Middle High German unzīt. By surface analysis, un- + Zeit.

pt: to put around, to hang around
noun:Umhängetasche.tx: From umhängen (“to put around, to hang around”) + Tasche (“bag”).

noun:Unbill.tx: Nominalised from Middle High German unbil (“inappropriate, unfair”), from Proto-West Germanic *bil(i) (“kind, gentle; decent, fair”).

noun:Undankbarkeit.tx: From undankbar + -keit; equivalent to un- + Dankbarkeit

adj:unlieb.tx: From Middle High German unliep, from Old High German unliob, from Proto-West Germanic *unleub, from Proto-Germanic *unleubaz. Equivalent to un- + lieb. Cognate with English unlief.

noun:Unreinheit.tx: From unrein (“impure”) + -heit. Further analysable as un- (“un-”) + rein (“pure”) + -heit (“-ness, -hood, -ty”).

noun:Unglaube.tx: From Middle High German ungloube, ungeloube, from Old High German ungiloubo, from Proto-West Germanic *ungalaubō, equivalent to un- + Glaube. Cognate with Dutch ongeloof, Saterland Frisian Uungloowe, Old English unġelēafa (whence English unbelief).

phrase:umgekehrt wird ein Schuh daraus.tx: Literally, “reverse is how it becomes a shoe”.

adv:überein.tx: Univerbation of über + ein. Compare Dutch overeen, Swedish överens.

phrase:u. A. w. g..tx: Abbreviation of um Antwort wird gebeten (“it is asked for an answer”, roughly).

noun:Unwort.tx: Inherited from Middle High German unwort, by surface analysis, un- + Wort.

verb:unterfangen.tx: From Middle High German undervāhen, from Old High German untarfāhan, from Proto-West Germanic *undarfą̄han. Equivalent to unter- + fangen. Cognate to Dutch ondervangen.

verb:überhören.tx: From Middle High German überhœren, uberhœren, equivalent to über- (“over-”) + hören (“hear”), but with a different meaning than English overhear. Compare also German Low German overhören, överhören.

noun:Uzi.tx: From English uzi with a spelling pronunciation, from Hebrew עוזי (uzi).

phrase:und wenn sie nicht gestorben sind.tx: Literally, “and if they haven’t died, they are still alive today”.

noun:Unglimpf.tx: From Middle High German ungelimpf. Equivalent to un- + Glimpf.

phrase:und ein paar Gequetschte.tx: Literally, “and some bruised ones”. Plausibly from such contexts as fruit harvesting, which yielded a certain saleable quantity plus some damaged ones for private consumption.

adv:umzu.tx: From um + zu, after Low German ümto.

verb:überwerfen.tx: From Middle High German überwërfen, from Old High German ubarwërfan. Equivalent to über (“over”) + werfen (“to throw”).

adj:übernächtigt.tx: From über- + nächtigen + -t or alternatively über- + nächtig + -t.

verb:untertunneln.tx: By surface analysis, unter- (“under”) + tunneln (“to tunnel”). Perhaps also directly derived from unter- + Tunnel + -n.

verb:umgraben.tx: From Middle High German umbegraben, from Old High German umbigraban. Equivalent to um- + graben. Cognate with Dutch omgraven.

verb:überleiten.tx: From Middle High German überleiten, from Old High German ubarleiten, from Proto-West Germanic *oberlaidijan, from Proto-Germanic *uberlaidijaną. Equivalent to über- + leiten. Cognates include Dutch overleiden and English overlead.

verb:unterheben.tx: From Middle High German underheben, from Old High German untarheffen, from Proto-West Germanic *underhabbjan. Equivalent to unter- + heben.

verb:untermalen.tx: From Middle High German undermālen. Equivalent to unter- + malen.

verb:untermischen.tx: From Middle High German undermischen, from Old High German untarmisken. Equivalent to unter- + mischen.

adj:ungezwungen.tx: From Middle High German ungetwungen. Equivalent to un- + gezwungen.

noun:Umstandsmode.tx: From Umstand + -s- + Mode, referring to the term in anderen Umständen (“pregnant”).

adv:übelst.tx: From übel + -st. Often framed as a neologism of the 2000s, but already in use by the 1980s.

adj:übermächtig.tx: From Middle High German übermehtic. By surface analysis, über- + -mächtig or Übermacht + -ig.

verb:übersenden.tx: From Middle High German übersenden. By surface analysis, über- + senden.

noun:Überlebenskünstler.tx: From Überlebenskunst + -ler. By surface analysis, Überleben + -s- + Künstler.

noun:Unfreiheit.tx: By surface analysis, un- + Freiheit or unfrei + -heit.

noun:Ulti.tx: Perhaps borrowed from English ultimate. Compare French ulti, Italian ulti, Spanish ulti, Portuguese ulti.
